claims.claim: The public session-context contract projects only entries on the supplied branch path: buildSessionContext(entries, undefined, BACKGROUND_CONTEXT) returns the ordered on-path messages and never off-path entries, which is the mechanism the restored-branch demo relies on.

The session-context test file defines the entry wire shape (id, parentId, seq, timestamp, type, message) through messageEntry, so a fixture can snapshot an entry tree and rebuild a restored branch by following parentId links.

The separate snapshot/restore fixture restores branch "main" from a captured tree with createForkSnapshot, and its restored branch tip is the terminal entry "snapshot-main-terminal" while the sibling leaf "snapshot-sibling-leaf" is dropped from the restored snapshot.

Projecting the restored branch path through buildSessionContext yields the terminal message ("main terminal response") and omits the sibling branch message ("sibling branch response"), while the whole-tree restore control keeps the sibling entry, proving the omission is due to branch-scoped restore and not fixture construction.

conclusion: A separate, standalone snapshot/restore fixture (packages/agent/test/harness/fixtures/session-snapshot-restore.fixture.ts) snapshots one session tree holding a shared root, a terminal entry on branch "main", and a sibling leaf on branch "sibling". Restoring only "main" via the production createForkSnapshot primitive produces a branch whose tip is the terminal entry "snapshot-main-terminal" and whose entry path is [snapshot-root, snapshot-main-terminal]. Projecting that path through buildSessionContext yields "main terminal response" (seesTerminalEntry=true) and never "sibling branch response" (seesSiblingEntry=false). The negative control—restoring the whole tree—retains the sibling leaf, proving the sibling omission is caused by branch-scoped restore. The fixture is executable with plain node and is also wired into a vitest wrapper.
